selected_object.owner: Core batch collection and public arrival metadata
selected_object.contract: IMessageBatch exposes actual first/last admission UTC. Public context TimeProvider is supported and defaults to system UTC. .NET UTC is wall-clock metadata, no increasing clock contract. ReviewI requires clock-jump correctness and distinguishing monotonic durations from UTC.
selected_object.trigger: Ordinary AddViciOneServiceBus, explicit limits, InMemory and batch MessageLimit2/TimeLimit5min. Middleware attaches a valid TimeProvider with system timers. After positively scheduled first admission at03:04:05 UTC, set UTC to03:03:05 and send second unique valid Item.
selected_object.actual: Both original message pipelines positively terminate with ArgumentOutOfRangeException(lastMessageReceived) from internal MessageBatch constructor; application batch consumer never called. Same configuration with forward UTC produces exact two identities, Size mode and one consumer invocation.
selected_object.expected: Deliver the two valid identities exactly once in one size-completed batch and retain true first/last admission UTC; backward wall-clock metadata must not turn valid messages into processing faults.

selected_object.recommendation: Prefer removing unsafe internal chronological UTC invariant; preserve first/last raw UTC semantics, all other constructor guards and exact message ordering. If actual duration is needed, expose it with TimeProvider.GetTimestamp/GetElapsedTime instead of UTC subtraction. Never silently clamp LastMessageReceived or change system clock.

No persistent migration.
